output.name: Halun

anatomy.part: tip of the beak, pointing up and out over the sea
the eye, set in the crown of the head
the breast, at the heart of the body
the underside of the wing, where the feathers meet the body
the wingtip, flung far out to the right
the right foot, tucked under the belly
the rump, where the tail begins
the tail tip, forked low on the left

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up and the sand-eels went down into the cold, and the puffins were left on the cliffs with empty bellies. Halun was the grey one who dove for them every morning. He came back with his beak full, a row of eels laid crossways like a net-line, and he said nothing. His chicks grew fat. Halun grew thin. Tavo the Gale saw him diving in a storm, laughed, and tore one of his wings wide, and still he came home. Hesk the Reel counted every eel he carried and never wrote his name down as a debt. When Halun reached the pole too tired to speak, Aun came down out of the lamps and took the eels from his beak one by one. Halun is up there still, mouth full. If a puffin comes low over the Reach with nothing said, you know it is him.
output.verse:
Grey beak, eels crossways
he comes home with his mouth full
and says nothing still
